title: Radiology Department Operations
thesis: Snowflake turns daily department-level activity from Harbourline Imaging, a synthetic Singapore imaging network, into study volume, turnaround and backlog KPIs, 7-day TAT breach risk scores, turnaround anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables, with no patient records or images.

talking_points: Study volume vs plan, reports outside the TAT target, average report turnaround and confirmed priority TAT breaches for 40 imaging departments across 5 Singapore planning areas: Novena, Jurong East, Tampines, Queenstown and Woodlands.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to department-day rows.
The delay-driver chart shows which worklist escalations turn into confirmed breaches and which are mostly cleared on review.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of radiology operations KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which departments should the workflow team look at first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each department's probability of a confirmed priority-study TAT breach in the next 7 days. It is an operational workflow score, not a diagnostic or clinical prediction.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags report turnaround outliers per department, and the forecast projects reports finalised in target for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

talking_points: Scanner QA compliance, QA certification coverage and pending certifications frame the equipment readiness gaps.
QA compliance against confirmed TAT breaches by department shows where missed QA checks and breaches move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised workflow actions from the KPI, department, delay-driver and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a long worklist wait lands right now?

talking_points: Live study-status events land in RAW.LIVE_STUDIES, from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe. They are department-level and carry no patient identifiers.
The Snowflake alert logs ALERT events with an SOP hint and the department's current risk band, then emails the radiology operations team.
tabs.call_out: From worklist event to follow-up in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 14 synthetic radiology workflow SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic, department-level demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
